newsitem.title: USA: Minn. hospital on track for conduit bond issuer.
newsitem.headline: Minn. hospital on track for conduit bond issuer.

text.p: A Minnesota health care system is on track to sell $175 million of tax-exempt bonds through a conduit state agency despite a pending bill that would prohibit the debt sale, a system official said Wednesday.

Mary Edwards, vice president of public policy for Fairview Health System, said the Minnesota Agricultural and Economic Development Board has given preliminary approval to the bond issue and has scheduled a final vote on the plan for April 9.

Proceeds from the bonds would mainly fund Fairview's acquisition of University of Minnesota Hospital and capital improvements at the facility. Smith Barney Inc. has been tapped as senior manager for the deal.

Edwards said a bill pending before the Minnesota Legislature that would retroactively ban the board from issuing bonds to finance a hospital acquisition will have no bearing on the deal other than disclosing the existance of the legislation.
Edwards said that Fairview has a "100 percent guarentee" from Gov. Arne Carlson that he would "never allow the bill to go through."
In fact, identical bills in the House and Senate appeared to be stalled in committee on Wednesday. The House sponsor of the bill was not available to comment.

Edwards said the bill was spurred by members of the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees, which is fighting Fairview before the National Labor Relations Board over representation of workers at the university hospital.
The union lost that representation when Fairview acquired the hospital in January.
Fairview turned to the Minnesota agency as a conduit bond issuer in February after the a Minneapolis City Council committee rejected the deal due to union pressure.
The health system needs to raise $87.5 million to pay off a promissory note due to expire June 30 that it issued for the university hospital.
Fairview officials have said they plan to insure the bonds through MBIA Insurance Corp.
